title: Initial Counting-Sort Placement State
statement: Let $A$ be counting-sort arguments, let $kf$ assign a key to each item index, and let $\mu'$ be an integer-valued memory map. Suppose that for every $t\le A.nb$, the cell at address $A.cnt+t$ contains the number of indices $i<A.n$ whose key is less than $t$, and that for every $t<A.nb$ with $A.nb\le t$, the cell at address $A.cnt+(t+1)$ contains the number of indices $i<A.n$ whose key equals $t$. Then for every $t<A.nb$, the cell at address $A.cnt+t$ contains the number of indices $i<A.n$ whose key is less than $t$, and for every $j<0$, the destination cell at the stable sorting position of item $j$ contains that item.
hypotheses_covered: Summed-count condition for each t ≤ A.nb
Equal-key count condition for each t < A.nb with A.nb ≤ t
replaced:
Let $A$ be a collection of counting-sort parameters, let $it,kf:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$
be functions, and let $\mu'$ be an integer-valued memory state. If, for every $t\le
A.nb$, the cell at address $A.cnt+t$ contains the number of indices below $A.n$ whose
key is less than $t$, and for every $t<A.nb$ with $A.nb\le t$, the cell at address
$A.cnt+(t+1)$ contains the number of indices below $A.n$ whose key equals $t$, then for
every $t<A.nb$ the cell at address $A.cnt+t$ contains the number of indices below $A.n$

indices below $0$ has its destination cell equal to the corresponding item value.
